issues.description: Image bytes converted with image.tobytes() without mode normalization will corrupt output for non-RGB images
issues.detail: The code does Image.open(io.BytesIO(part.inline_data.data)) then image.tobytes() and hardcodes format="RGB". PIL's tobytes() returns raw pixel bytes in the image's actual mode (could be RGBA, P, L, etc. depending on what Gemini returns). If the decoded image is not already RGB, the consumer reading those bytes as RGB will get scrambled colors or a size mismatch. The data structure is wrong here: either convert with image.convert("RGB") before tobytes(), or pass the raw encoded bytes through and let the sink decode. Right now the algorithm is fighting the data shape.

issues.description: Monkey-patching genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE at import time is the wrong shape
issues.detail: Mutating a private attribute of a third-party module at import time is global, hidden state with no scope. The comment even calls it a "temporary hack." This belongs at the call site (configure the client with appropriate http options) or behind a feature flag tied to image models only, not as a side effect of importing the module. As written, any other code in the process that uses google-genai inherits this 5MB buffer whether it wants to or not.

issues.description: Image branch is buried inside a deeply nested for/if cascade that wants to be a filter
issues.detail: _process_context walks candidates -> content.parts -> branches on text / function_call / inline_data inside an already long method. Each part type is a small stateless transform from a Gemini Part into an outbound Frame. This is textbook filter shape: a small dispatch table or a handful of part-to-frame functions composed together would make each new modality (image, audio, video) a one-line addition instead of another elif in a growing pyramid. The data (Part) dominates; pick the right structure and the algorithm becomes obvious.

issues.description: Default model bump is a behavior change disguised as a feature add
issues.detail: Changing the default from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash silently alters cost, latency, and output characteristics for every existing caller who relied on the default. The CHANGELOG notes it under Changed, which is correct, but this deserves its own consideration separate from the image-generation feature; bundling them couples two unrelated decisions in one PR.

issues.description: String-substring model gating ("image" in self._model_name) is fragile
issues.detail: Using `"image" in self._model_name` to detect image-generation models is a substring sniff that will misfire the day Google ships a model whose name happens to contain that token for unrelated reasons, or miss a future image model named differently. A small set or a capability flag on a model-config struct would be the right data structure. Minor today, but the wrong shape for something that will grow.

issues.description: Stray blank line in __init__ adds no signal
issues.detail: An empty line was added between self._http_options assignment and self._create_client. Not wrong, just noise in the diff; the kind of incidental change worth dropping so the diff says exactly what it means.

review.summary: The feature is small and the diff is mostly the right size, but the image handling has the wrong data structure: PIL's tobytes() with a hardcoded RGB format will silently corrupt non-RGB outputs, and the part-dispatch cascade in _process_context wants to be a small filter table rather than another elif. The monkey-patch of genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE at import time is global hidden state and should move to client configuration. The default-model change and the "image" substring check are minor shape issues worth tightening. Decision: TOO-CLEVER / WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE on the image branch; the rest is close to SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE once those are fixed.
